title: 系围裙的将军  (General in an Apron)

segments.t: At six o'clock Wednesday morning, warm light fills the kitchen where Mei sits comfortably with her ankle propped on two pillows, tapping a wooden spoon like a baton for Peng and Qing. Let's listen in first.
志鹏，用手掌根往下推，折一次，转半圈，再推！
收到，主厨！现在的面团看起来怎么样？
又光滑又柔软，按下去马上弹回来——放进温碗里盖上湿布！
小美，四个蛋黄、新鲜柠檬汁，还有糖罐里的三勺糖！
小晴，开小火不停地搅——千万别让锅底煮开了！
小美，今天早上你的脚踝感觉怎么样？
说真的？多亏你们俩不让我下地，已经消肿一半了！
快看，金黄的柠檬酱变得多浓稠、多亮呀！
马上关火！放一块冰的无盐黄油进去搅匀！
闻闻这股清爽的柠檬热气，整个一楼都是香味！
二十个酥脆的杏仁挞底已经在晾架上排好了！
一点儿也不错，两位徒弟——我的面包房交给你们放心了！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
志鹏，用手掌根往下推，折一次，转半圈，再推！

'Push down with the heel of your hand, Peng, fold once, turn halfway, push again!' Mei fires off brisk baking orders from her pillows. Where English says "the heel of your hand", Mandarin says "palm-root".
收到，主厨！现在的面团看起来怎么样？
'Got it, chef! How does the dough look now?' Peng salutes with the brisk two-character word meaning "received!", how staff answer a radio call or head cook. "Dough" joins "flour" with "round ball".
又光滑又柔软，按下去马上弹回来——放进温碗里盖上湿布！

'Smooth and soft, and springing right back—into the warm bowl under a damp cloth!' Repeating the little word for "both" before two qualities—"both smooth and soft"—is Mandarin's favourite way to pair two good traits.
小美，四个蛋黄、新鲜柠檬汁，还有糖罐里的三勺糖！
'Four egg yolks, fresh lemon juice, and three spoons of sugar from the sugar jar, Mei!' Mandarin names parts of an egg simply by colour: "egg-yellow" is the yolk, while "egg-white" is the white.
小晴，开小火不停地搅——千万别让锅底煮开了！

'Keep whisking over low heat, Qing—never let the bottom of the pot boil!' Where English cooks say "low heat", Mandarin says "small fire". And "ten thousand" before "don't" adds urgent emphasis: "whatever you do, don't!"
小美，今天早上你的脚踝感觉怎么样？
'How is your ankle feeling this morning, Mei?' Mandarin always orders time from biggest to smallest—"today" first, then "morning"—zooming in on the moment step by step.
说真的？多亏你们俩不让我下地，已经消肿一半了！

'Honestly? Half the swelling is gone already thanks to you two keeping me off my feet!' Mei's two-word opener literally asks "speaking for real?" And "keeping me off my feet" is put plainly as "not letting me step on the ground".
快看，金黄的柠檬酱变得多浓稠、多亮呀！
'Look how thick and glossy the golden lemon curd just turned!' Putting that little word for "how" before each quality turns a statement into an exclamation—"how thick, how bright!"
马上关火！放一块冰的无盐黄油进去搅匀！

'Turn off the flame right away! Stir in one cold cube of unsalted butter!' Look at "unsalted butter": "without-salt yellow-oil". Joining "stir" with "even" at the end means mix until completely smooth.
闻闻这股清爽的柠檬热气，整个一楼都是香味！
'Smell that bright lemon steam—the whole ground floor is filled with fragrance!' In Mandarin, just like in American English, "first floor" refers to the ground level at street height.
二十个酥脆的杏仁挞底已经在晾架上排好了！
'Twenty crisp almond tart shells are lined up ready on the cooling rack!' "Cooling rack" uses a specific kitchen word meaning "air-cool in the breeze", separate from chilling food on ice.
一点儿也不错，两位徒弟——我的面包房交给你们放心了！
'Not bad at all, apprentices—my bakery is in safe hands with you!' Mei closes with the warm everyday word for "reassured", built literally out of "set down your heart".
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
志鹏，用手掌根往下推，折一次，转半圈，再推！
收到，主厨！现在的面团看起来怎么样？
又光滑又柔软，按下去马上弹回来——放进温碗里盖上湿布！
小美，四个蛋黄、新鲜柠檬汁，还有糖罐里的三勺糖！
小晴，开小火不停地搅——千万别让锅底煮开了！
小美，今天早上你的脚踝感觉怎么样？
说真的？多亏你们俩不让我下地，已经消肿一半了！
快看，金黄的柠檬酱变得多浓稠、多亮呀！
马上关火！放一块冰的无盐黄油进去搅匀！
闻闻这股清爽的柠檬热气，整个一楼都是香味！
二十个酥脆的杏仁挞底已经在晾架上排好了！
一点儿也不错，两位徒弟——我的面包房交给你们放心了！
Under Mei's watchful eye, the bread dough rises and glossy lemon curd fills twenty golden tarts. See you next time.
回头见！
